what_happened: orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's existing group_by(.class) aggregation and the null-resolution-reads-as-open coalescing (with implicit_open_count) were found already implemented and correct on direct source read, which resolved two of the task's open research questions (the collapse-signal concern and task 562's boundary) without any new code -- confirms the issue-log/conclusion-stage machinery is a stronger reuse target than initially assumed from the dispatch description alone.

errors-append.sh's 'append' subcommand (the write half of the documented error-handling contract in rules/error-handling.md) was mechanically verified to have zero production call sites across agents/skills/hooks/commands/scripts in the source store -- every reference is a comment, a test fixture, or verify-deploy.sh's manifest-presence check. This confirms the dispatch's 'nothing writes it' claim directly rather than trusting it, and settles that correcting rules/error-handling.md's pointer (rather than reviving the store) is the lower-cost remedy.

The research report settled all seven design questions but stopped short of two details that block implementation of its own decision 6: sapience-retrieve.sh exits 1 identically for a genuine transport/HTTP failure and for a benign zero-hit search, so capturing 'the body it already holds' without flooding every task log requires an exit-code split plus curl --write-out; and issue-log.md's seed class enum is duplicated in issue-record.sh as ISSUE_SEED_CLASSES plus a usage-comment copy, so adding the new class is a two-file change, not a documentation edit. Both were resolved during planning and specified in the plan's Research Integration section rather than left for the implementer to discover.

Sourcing scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh and running suite_selection_select over each candidate path produced measured, verbatim-citable Tier Justifications for all six non-final phases in one batch, instead of guessing at covering checks. It also surfaced a reusable planning fact: any extension manifest.json maps to a ~31-suite structural set, so a phase that registers a new script in a manifest is honestly a full-tier phase rather than a cheap one.

Plan phase 1's Verification lists 'verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4' as a pass/fail check, but gate 3's Rule F (deployed-script-content-drift) and the index-entries.json line-count check both compare against the DEPLOYED tree, which the plan's own Standing Note says is not redeployed until Phase 7. Confirmed by direct measurement: before this phase's edits, core had zero doc-lint FAILs; after editing issue-log.md and issue-record.sh in the source store only, gate 3 shows 'deployed script content drift: scripts/issue-record.sh' and an index-entries.json line_count mismatch for issue-log.md (205 declared vs 275 actual) -- both caused purely by the pending-deploy gap, not a real defect in the edit. generate-context-line-counts.sh itself refuses to run from the source store, confirming the fix requires a deploy. Deferring both to Phase 7's redeploy + full gate run; this phase's content-level verification (diff read-through, the run-all.sh suite subset) is otherwise green.
